q.intro.text: A club splits its two hundred forty dollar budget between art and music, in the ratio three to five. Art spends twenty percent of its share on paint. How much does art spend on paint? Pick an answer, and say how sure you are.

q.cb.right.text: At the start you picked eighteen dollars, and you were right. Now you can say why: the percent step's whole was art's share.

q.cb.whole.text: At the start you picked forty-eight dollars. That is twenty percent of the whole budget. The paint comes out of art's share, so its whole was ninety dollars.

q.cb.other.text: At the start you picked twenty-eight dollars and eighty cents. That reads three to five as three fifths of the budget. Art gets three of every eight parts.

q.cb.none.text: Name the whole of every percent step. It can be the result of the step before.

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the tapes move first, then the notation.

e.step0.text: Three to five is a ratio step: it shares the budget. Twenty percent is a percent step, and its whole is art's share, not the two hundred forty dollars. The percent step needs art's share, so the ratio step goes first.

e.step1.text: Three plus five is eight equal parts, and two hundred forty dollars divided by eight is thirty dollars a part. Art gets three parts: ninety dollars. Music gets the other five: a hundred fifty dollars.

e.step2.text: Art's ninety dollars is the new whole: it fills the whole tape, one hundred percent. Twenty percent of it is zero point two times ninety, which is eighteen dollars for paint.

e.step3.text: Check against the story, not by redoing the arithmetic. Eighteen dollars is twenty percent of ninety. And ninety and a hundred fifty add to two hundred forty, in the ratio three to five.

e.why.text: Quick check: why is the paint twenty percent of ninety dollars, and not twenty percent of two hundred forty?

e.why.ok.text: Yes. Every percent step has its own whole. This one is art's share.

e.why.whole.text: Look at the top tape. Twenty percent of two hundred forty dollars is forty-eight dollars, more than half of art's ninety. The story says twenty percent of art's share.

e.why.order.text: Story order isn't the reason. The percent step says of its share, so it needs art's share. That sets the order.

t.intro.text: A bag holds thirty-six ounces of trail mix, nuts to raisins seven to two. Twenty-five percent of the nuts are almonds. How many ounces of almonds? The first two steps are done for you.

t.whole.text: The almonds are twenty-five percent of which amount? Pick the whole for this step.

t.whole.ok.text: Yes. Twenty-five percent of the nuts. The twenty-eight ounces of nuts is one hundred percent for this step.

t.whole.mix.text: Watch. Twenty-five percent of thirty-six ounces is nine ounces, a quarter of the whole bag, raisins too. The almonds are twenty-five percent of the nuts.

t.whole.raisins.text: The raisins are the other part. Almonds are nuts.

t.alm.text: How many ounces of almonds? Use the new whole.

t.alm.ok.text: Yes. Zero point two five times twenty-eight is seven. Seven ounces of almonds.

t.alm.mix.text: Nine ounces is twenty-five percent of the whole bag. Use the nuts: twenty-five percent of twenty-eight ounces.

t.alm.raisins.text: Two ounces is twenty-five percent of the raisins. The almonds are twenty-five percent of the nuts.

t.alm.rest.text: Twenty-one ounces is the other seventy-five percent of the nuts. The almonds are the twenty-five percent.

t.alm.nuts.text: Twenty-eight ounces is all the nuts: the whole. The almonds are twenty-five percent of it.

t.alm.no.text: Twenty-five percent is one quarter. What is one quarter of twenty-eight ounces?

t.check.text: Check it against the story. Seven ounces is what percent of twenty-eight ounces?

t.check.ok.text: Seven divided by twenty-eight is zero point two five, which is twenty-five percent. It matches the story, so seven ounces is right.

t.check.flip.text: That is twenty-eight divided by seven. The percent is the part divided by the whole: seven divided by twenty-eight.

t.check.mix.text: That compares with the whole bag. Check against the nuts: seven divided by twenty-eight.

t.check.no.text: Divide the part by its whole, seven divided by twenty-eight, then write it as a percent.

p.intro.text: Maya buys an eighty dollar jacket that is twenty-five percent off. Then eight percent sales tax is added to the sale price. Maya says: minus twenty-five percent and plus eight percent make minus seventeen percent, so I pay eighty-three percent of eighty dollars, which is sixty-six dollars and forty cents. Is Maya right?

p.test.text: Let's test it. Build the argument, and see where it leads.

p.build.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.no.adds.text: They only add when both are percents of the same whole. Here the tax is a percent of the smaller sale price.

p.no.arith.text: Her arithmetic is right, but her setup uses the wrong whole for the tax. Right arithmetic can't fix a wrong setup.

p.no.tag.text: The story says the tax is added to the sale price. The whole is whatever the step says.

p.no.other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line. Which reason makes this line true?

p.c1.text: Right. After the discount, the whole changes. The tax's whole is the sale price, so Maya's lines fall apart.

p.c2.text: Right. Seventy-five percent of eighty dollars is sixty dollars. That is the new whole, one hundred percent for the tax.

p.c3.text: Right. Eight percent of sixty dollars is four dollars and eighty cents, so the total is sixty-four dollars and eighty cents. Maya's sixty-six forty is too much.

p.done.text: That's a proof: three claims, each with its reason, and the tapes back every one. Percents of different wholes can't simply be added.
